clue.text: Hot spice sick one quietly put in soup

indicators.note: put in tells us the following pieces go inside the soup

parts.note: chowder is a thick soup, often of fish or clams
sick means ill
one is the Roman numeral I
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A cook adds a fiery spice to a soup for someone feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is the insertion signal; P for quietly comes from musical notation (piano).
explanation.definitionFit: Ground dried chillies make a fiery seasoning, so it is a hot spice by description.

clue.text: Pry about argument with lawyers

definitions.note: here a noun, a lever, as in a pry bar

parts.note: C is circa, about
a row is a quarrel
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Someone noses into a quarrel involving lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pry' reads as a verb for snooping but here is the tool used to lever things open.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is an iron lever used to force things open, which is what a pry is.

clue.text: Current agreement is unsurpassed

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: The present arrangement can't be bettered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes the perfect, so something that cannot be bettered.

clue.text: Despair at roles he messed up

indicators.note: messed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor is downcast at having bungled the parts he played.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to become discouraged and give up hope.

clue.text: Send message to part of website

definitions.meaning: to summon someone over a ... or loudspeaker
a single screen of a site

explanation.surface: Someone contacts a section of a website.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to call them; a web page is one document on a site.

clue.text: Who'd act barking? Guard, primarily

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are scrambled
primarily takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A riddle: which creature would bark, mainly as a guard?
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' rearranges WHODACT; 'primarily' gives G from Guard. The whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard dog barks to warn off intruders, and it would act this way.

clue.text: Bird repeatedly shaking wings in heat, ugly hen

indicators.note: shaking off the wings of each word in turn removes its outer letters

explanation.surface: A homely hen flaps about in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping first and last letters gives EA, GL and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Young Jack starts to use vessel on European river

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: the Nile is an African river

explanation.surface: A boy called Jack begins to sail a boat on a European river.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenile means youthful or not yet adult.

clue.text: Know no uprising in African land

definitions.note: used attributively: of the African land

parts.note: ken is Scots for know

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: nay means no

explanation.surface: No revolt is recognised in a nation of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' signals reversal in a down clue; KEN for know is Scots and Northern English.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to Kenya, a country of East Africa.

clue.text: Blunder of six deliveries location reported

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

indicators.note: reported says we want a word that is spoken like the word for location

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes an error where six balls were bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER in cricket is a set of six deliveries by one bowler; SITE said out loud gives SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made through failing to notice something, a blunder.

clue.text: Look to secure universal thin fabric

indicators.note: to secure means to hold something within, so the look wraps round the letter

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Someone is told to inspect a fastening on lightweight cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts U inside GAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauze is a light, open-weave cloth, as used for dressings and veils.

clue.text: Awkward throw returned by another

indicators.note: returned tells us the word for throw is read backwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw high
another throw: to shy is to fling

explanation.surface: One throw is sent back and followed by a second toss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LOB into BOL; 'another' means another throw, SHY, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang for uncooperative or rebellious, so awkward in temperament.

clue.text: Article about this writer and really criminal act

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the article goes round the writer

parts.note: the is the definite article
this writer is the setter, I
really means very

explanation.surface: A news piece about the author and a genuinely criminal deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the article wraps round I; 'this writer' is the setter referring to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Thievery is the practice of stealing, which is a crime.

clue.text: Again, go over adult's tips on two school subjects

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
the second school subject, PE, physical education

indicators.note: tips are the ends, so the first and last letters of adult are taken

explanation.surface: A pupil revises the extremes of grown-up topics in two lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two school subjects' supplies RE and PE; 'tips' takes the outer letters of 'adult', A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat something is to go over it once more, doing it again.

clue.text: Performer in part, thespian is terrible

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actor is partly judged to be dreadful on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianiste is a female pianist, a musician who plays to an audience.

clue.text: Notice for travellers at sea: boarding's not starting

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not starting removes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Passengers on a ship are told about embarkation procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops the B of BOARDINGS; 'at sea' rearranges OARDINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A road sign is a posted notice giving directions or warnings to drivers.

clue.text: Issue detective's accusation

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, plus the S
a charge is a formal accusation

explanation.surface: A police officer brings a charge against someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge is to let out or emit, to issue.

clue.text: Fools set up with trap good for robbing

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: nits are fools in British slang
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Idiots are set up and caught by a trap for robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses NITS to STIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinging is slang for overcharging or swindling someone, robbing them.

clue.text: Number in St Kitts regularly filling wharf

indicators.note: filling says these letters go inside the word for wharf

parts.note: a quay is a wharf

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A tally taken at a Caribbean island's dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of 'in St Kitts', NTIT, and 'filling' puts them in QUAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity is an amount or count, a number of things.

clue.text: Cats playing cards somewhere in New York

definitions.meaning: the court cards ranking between king and jack
a borough of New York City

explanation.surface: Felines play a card game in a New York neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens are breeding female cats, court cards, and a borough of New York City.

clue.text: Value eastern links to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left

parts.note: to meet is to join up, link

explanation.surface: The East forms connections with the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' reverses MEETS to STEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something is to prize it, to value it highly.

clue.text: Notes explosives around exterior of U-boat

indicators.note: around says the explosives surround the other letters

parts.note: mines are explosive devices

indicators.note: exterior of takes the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Mines are laid around the hull of a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior of' gives U and T from U-boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutes are the written record or notes of a meeting.

clue.text: Ecstasy developed in happy realisation

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled moment of joyful insight.
explanation.walkthrough: E is a common abbreviation for the drug ecstasy; 'developed' rearranges IN HAPPY to PIPHANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden moment of insight or understanding.

clue.text: Back international language

parts.note: hind means at the back

explanation.surface: Support for a worldwide tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is a major language of India.

clue.text: Pitched support for monarch on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so we want a soundalike

parts.note: a king sits on a throne, which supports them

explanation.surface: A broadcast about a royal backer being promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitched as in a ball delivered: thrown is the past participle of throw.

clue.text: Award Yankee son accepts

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire
Y in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American's son takes an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey an order is to comply with it, accepting it.

clue.text: Personality from France, the French revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: F is the international code for France
les is French for the

explanation.surface: A personality emerges from the French revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses FLES.
explanation.definitionFit: One's self is one's identity or character, personality.

clue.text: It's unacceptable either way

definitions.note: the two-word phrase for out of order reads identically from either end

indicators.note: either way says the letters read the same from both ends

parts.note: the two-word phrase for out of order reads identically from either end

explanation.surface: Someone declares a thing out of order whichever way it is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase not on is British idiom for not acceptable.

clue.text: Seriously close to home on island

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the pieces after the island letter

parts.note: near means close
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone means it about living near home on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'X on Y' puts X after Y, so the island comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in earnest is doing it with sincerity, seriously.

clue.text: Lion feasting after playing with boks

indicators.note: playing means fooling about with them, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A lion gorges on antelope after a game with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Boks are antelopes such as springboks; 'playing' rearranges FEASTING and BOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is traditionally called the monarch of the animal world.
